title: 10 Documentary Collection & Letter of Credit - Topic Quiz

questions.text: Who is the applicant in a Letter of Credit, and who initiates a Documentary Collection?
options: Exporter for a Letter of Credit; importer for a Documentary Collection
Importer for a Letter of Credit; exporter for a Documentary Collection
Always the importer in both payment methods
Always the freight forwarder in both payment methods
questions.correctAnswer: Importer for a Letter of Credit; exporter for a Documentary Collection

questions.text: Which residual risk remains with the importer in BOTH a Letter of Credit and a Documentary Collection?
options: That banks never inspect any shipping documents
That the goods are defective, because banks check only documents and never physical goods
That the Letter of Credit is amended unilaterally by the exporter without consent
That the importer must pay cash before the goods are shipped
questions.correctAnswer: That the goods are defective, because banks check only documents and never physical goods

questions.text: How do an unconfirmed Letter of Credit and a confirmed Letter of Credit differ regarding bank liability?
options: Unconfirmed: only the buyer's issuing bank is liable; confirmed: the seller's bank is also liable
Unconfirmed: no bank is liable; confirmed: only the buyer's bank is liable
Unconfirmed: only the seller's bank is liable; confirmed: the freight forwarder is liable
In both forms, both banks are automatically liable in equal shares
questions.correctAnswer: Unconfirmed: only the buyer's issuing bank is liable; confirmed: the seller's bank is also liable

questions.text: If no specific presentation period is stated in a Letter of Credit, what is the default maximum number of days after the shipment date to present transport documents?
options: 7 days
10 days
30 days
21 days

questions.text: Why is a Documentary Collection significantly riskier for the exporter than a Letter of Credit?
options: Because there is no bank payment guarantee, so non-acceptance and transfer risks remain with the exporter
Because the exporter is legally required to pay all bank fees alone
Because the importer receives the shipping documents without payment or bill acceptance
Because Documentary Collection is permitted only for orders above EUR 100,000
questions.correctAnswer: Because there is no bank payment guarantee, so non-acceptance and transfer risks remain with the exporter

questions.text: What is the difference between Documentary Collection D/P and D/A?
options: D/P grants a payment term via bill of exchange; D/A requires immediate cash payment
D/P is a confirmed Letter of Credit; D/A is an unconfirmed Letter of Credit
D/P applies only to air freight; D/A applies only to ocean shipping
D/P releases documents against simultaneous payment; D/A releases documents against acceptance of a bill of exchange
questions.correctAnswer: D/P releases documents against simultaneous payment; D/A releases documents against acceptance of a bill of exchange

questions.text: Honigmayr GmbH sells honey worth EUR 8,500.00 to the well-known Novotel hotel chain in Berlin (EU). Which payment method is most suitable?
options: A confirmed Letter of Credit due to very high country risk
Full payment in advance before production due to lack of trust
Documentary Collection D/P because of a trusted partner, low country risk, and moderate order value
An escrow account located outside the European Union
questions.correctAnswer: Documentary Collection D/P because of a trusted partner, low country risk, and moderate order value

questions.text: Under ICC Paris UCP rules, every Letter of Credit is irrevocable and time-limited.
Under a Letter of Credit, the involved banks personally inspect the quality and quantity of the physical goods at the port.
Compare a Letter of Credit and a Documentary Collection across applicant, bank payment guarantee, exporter's risk of non-acceptance, and best use case.
questions.correctAnswer: Applicant: Letter of Credit = importer (buyer), Documentary Collection = exporter (seller). Bank guarantee: Letter of Credit gives an irrevocable bank payment promise (plus advising bank if confirmed); Documentary Collection has no bank guarantee. Non-acceptance risk: covered for the exporter under a Letter of Credit, but remains with the exporter (along with transfer risk) under Documentary Collection. Best use case: Letter of Credit for new partners, high order values, and higher country risk; Documentary Collection for trusted partners and low country risk (cheaper and simpler).
